low_light.text: Convert this image into a realistic and distinctly challenging low-light capture during the deep blue hour shortly after sunset, near the transition from civil twilight to nautical twilight. The drone region has been visually masked or blurred in the input image. Do not generate, add, duplicate, or hallucinate any drone, aircraft, bird, or flying object. Fill the masked drone area naturally as part of the surrounding low-light background. Preserve the exact camera viewpoint, scene identity, mountains, buildings, roads, skyline, all existing object locations, and all large-scale scene geometry. Reduce the exposure substantially, approximately like a photograph underexposed by two and a quarter to two and three-quarter stops. Transform ordinary daylight into a convincingly dim post-sunset environment with weak, diffuse blue-gray ambient illumination. The exposure reduction must be clearly stronger than an overcast-day or ordinary-dusk edit. Use a deep blue-gray sky and strongly subdued scene illumination. Compress the midtones, darken vegetation and building faces substantially, and place much of the terrain and urban foreground in deep but nonzero shadow. Major mountain contours, building masses, road geometry, and a limited amount of surface texture must remain faintly recoverable. Small low-contrast objects should become meaningfully harder to detect. This must look like a real photograph captured at the edge of night, not like a global brightness filter. Maintain spatially coherent exposure, natural tonal roll-off, plausible shadow relationships, and realistic camera response throughout the image. Do not produce a fully black night scene, a black sky, or large featureless crushed-black regions. Do not erase roads, buildings, mountains, or other major scene structure. Do not add new street lamps, illuminated windows, vehicles, or artificial light sources. Preserve only lights that already exist in the original scene. Do not add rain, snow, fog, haze, dust, foreground particles, motion blur, strong backlight, lens flare, sunset glow, orange coloration, or unrelated semantic objects.
